material_definitions: Simple cubic perovskite La(0.67-x)Li(3x)TiO3 (where x = 0.06 200.15) with disordered arrangement of the A-site ions was prepared by quenching from 1350 000C into liquid N2.
The tetragonal, doubled perovskite form (a = ap, c  224 2ap) features alternate arrangement of La-rich layers and Li-vacancy-rich layers along the c-axis.
The ordered form was created by annealing the quenched pellet at 800 000C for 3 days.
The study compares the conductivity of these disordered and ordered polymorphs.
The materials studied are lithium ion conducting perovskite solid solutions, focusing on compositions around x=0.12.
The samples exist in two main phases: a cubic, disordered form (achieved by quenching) and a tetragonal, ordered form (achieved by annealing).
The cubic form has a simple perovskite unit cell (S.G: Pm 	bar{3} m) where La ions, Li ions, and vacancies are randomly distributed over the A-sites.
The ordered form adopts a tetragonal, doubled cell (P4/mmm) characterized by alternate arrangement of La-rich layers and Li-vacancy-rich layers along the c-axis.
The study found the maximum conductivity at x = 0.12 for both forms.

The material series discussed is polycrystalline La(0.67-x)Li(3x)TiO3 (where x > 0.08).
The study compares the ionic conductivity of the tetragonal form (order parameter S ≈ 0.5-0.7) and the simple cubic form.
The simple cubic form with x = 0.12 showed a maximum bulk conductivity for the known perovskite solid solutions.
The lower conductivity in the tetragonal form is attributed to an increase in activation energy associated with contraction in the a-axis.
